title: LASER-seq: Transcriptome-wide RNA solvent accessibility mapping using photoactivated chemical probing
key_innovation: Compared with conventional chemical probing approaches, LASER-seq introduces a photoactivated NAz probe that forms C8 nucleobase adducts on accessible purines, enabling transcriptome-wide measurement of RNA solvent accessibility through reverse transcription stops or mutation-based readouts.

blocks.text: How does LASER-seq convert photoactivated chemical modification into RNA structure information?

blocks.alt: Principle and workflow of LASER-seq chemical probing
blocks.legend: **Figure 1. Principle and workflow of LASER-seq chemical probing.** Nicotinoyl azide (NAz) is activated by long-wavelength UV irradiation to generate reactive intermediates that form C8 adducts on adenine and guanine residues. These modifications alter reverse transcription, producing either RT-stop signals (LASER-seq) or nucleotide misincorporations (LASER-MaP). Following NAz probing, RNA is extracted, fragmented, reverse transcribed, and converted into sequencing libraries for transcriptome-wide structure analysis.
blocks.label: LASER-seq F1

blocks.text: How does LASER-seq convert photoactivated chemical modification into RNA structure information?

blocks.alt: Detection of NAz modification through RT stops and mutation signatures
blocks.legend: **Figure 2. Detection of NAz modification through RT stops and mutation signatures.** LASER-seq detects NAz-induced modifications through reverse transcription termination, whereas LASER-MaP converts these modifications into mutation signatures. Comparison between NAz-treated and untreated samples reveals modification-dependent signals at nucleotide resolution, demonstrating the specificity of LASER-based probing.
blocks.label: LASER-seq F2

blocks.text: How does LASER-seq report RNA solvent accessibility in structured RNAs?

blocks.alt: NAz reactivity reflects nucleotide solvent accessibility
blocks.legend: **Figure 3. NAz reactivity reflects nucleotide solvent accessibility.** LASER-MaP reactivity correlates with experimentally determined solvent accessibility of ribosomal RNA structures. NAz-derived modification patterns accurately identify exposed nucleotides, demonstrating that LASER-seq reports RNA surface accessibility rather than backbone flexibility measured by SHAPE chemistry.
blocks.label: LASER-seq F3
